## Phase B: targeted expansion complete

The original 176 lesson/project challenges and 48 bank questions are preserved. Phase B adds 23 independent questions, bringing the inventory to **247 unique questions**, **232 practice-ready**, and **71 independent bank problems**. The six tracks keep their existing question lists.

| Batch | IDs | New skill and distinguishing edge cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query optimization (4) | qb-0049–0052 | Equality/range composite keys, covering access, SARGable day filtering, reverse index traversal without temporary sorting |
| Funnels and sessions (5) | qb-0053–0057 | Ordered same-cart funnels, attempt-level abandonment, conflicting retries, strict inactivity boundaries, first-touch session conversion |
| Database engineering (3) | qb-0058–0060 | Versioned idempotent UPSERT, clean-before-dedupe constraints with valid/invalid write probes, recovery across stock and audit state |
| Many-to-many (3) | qb-0061–0063 | Unordered basket pairs, dynamic relational division, membership-set Jaccard overlap |
| Text parsing (3) | qb-0064–0066 | Whole-token code validation, explicit email normalization boundaries, decimal grammar and exact integer cents |
| Connected analytics case (5) | qb-0067–0071 | Daily session baseline, ordered funnel drop-off, nearest-rank latency p90, later-session recovery, unresolved channel priority |

### Quality gates

The first optimization question was validated independently before the remaining three were authored. Each of the six batches was checked before proceeding to the next. Every reference solution runs against visible and changed fixtures; negative tests reject meaningful wrong approaches, and independent expected-value tests check important semantics separately from reference-vs-reference comparison.

Optimization problems check declared behavior on controlled data, **not universal query speed**. Only qb-0052 requires avoiding temporary sorts; none uses `noFullScans`. The deployed local SQLite assets remain version 3.49.1. Schema and plan contracts are detailed in [PLAN_VALIDATION.md](../PLAN_VALIDATION.md).

The load grader executes the full script twice on each fixture. Engineering tasks also compare complete affected/source-table query results against an independently executed reference database. Constraints are tested with invalid writes and a valid insert, all rolled back. Recovery is evaluated through both final stock balances and audit state.

### Case-study execution model

The five checkout-review stages form a connected business narrative, but **each stage starts with a fresh database** and recomputes its intermediates from `market_web_events`. Stage navigation does not transfer SQL tables or result artifacts. Progress stays in canonical independent question records; the case study does not create a seventh track or affect lesson/project mastery.

## Remaining opportunities

- Partial/expression index objectives and explicit collation/direction requirements need additional plan contracts and controlled fixtures before authoring.
- Cross-database SQL dialects, optimizer timing benchmarks and universal performance scores remain out of scope.
- The 22 repeated lesson pairs remain a curriculum/migration decision; original lesson content was not rewritten.
- Assess track placement after learners have used the new questions. A dedicated optimization track is an option to evaluate, not an automatically added track.
- A future domain such as support-ticket SLA analysis could diversify the bank. This phase deliberately reuses and extends Harbor Market.
